newsitem.title: UK: Copper stabilises above $1,900, others firmer.
newsitem.headline: Copper stabilises above $1,900, others firmer.

text.p: Copper settled at firmer levels on Wednesday afternoon after being whipped around over the past few days, leaving some traders confounded about future direction.

Three months prices stabilised above the $1,900-a-tonne benchmark in thin London Metal Exchange (LME) afternoon trade after shooting to nearly $2,000 last Friday and slumping to $1,875 in inter-office business late on Tuesday.
Last business on Wednesday's kerb was at $1,918, up $28 from Tuesday and just off a high of $1,922.
"I'm standing aside at the moment. I just can't get a handle on the market," one floor trader said.
Volumes have been mostly lacklustre recently as traders struggle to figure out whether much Sumitomo material is still overhanging the market and how the fundamentals will pan out.
"There was one 100-lot deal yesterday, but mostly we've been seeing eight or nine lots at a go these days," a trader said.

Some traders say physical offtake remains healthy after tightness briefly pushed the market into backwardation last week. Inventories fell by 7,825 tonnes on Tuesday, but some analysts believe stocks are due to start rising again.
Copper and other base metals were little moved by the October options declaration at around 1030 GMT.
The other metals largely followed copper higher after Tuesday's rout, but aluminium remained trapped below $1,400.
Aluminium recovered from a fresh 2-1/4 year low on Tuesday, finishing $9.50 firmer at $1,377.
Nickel also managed a healthy bounce, probing the $7,100 barrier on the kerb and ending $90 higher at $7,095 after retesting the downside earlier in the day, bottoming at $6,970.
Tin also rebounded after Tuesday's plunge to a low of $5,900, finishing $65 stronger at $6,040.
Lead ended at $760, up $3 from the previous close and well off Tuesday's nadir of $745.
Zinc, which has remained a pillar of stability while the others flopped about, finished the kerb at $1,021, up $2 and well within the range of the past week.
Last business in alloy was off $5 at $1,225.
